title: British Embassy France Internships 2026 | Apply for Internship Opportunities in Paris
summary: The British Embassy in France is inviting applications for three full-time internship positions in Paris , offering an opportunity to gain practical experience in diplomacy, international affairs, public policy, communications, national security and UK-France relations. The internships are available across three teams: Economics and Political Section (EPS), National Security and Foreign Policy Section (NSFP), and the Communications and Engagement Team . Applicants can indicate their preferred team during the application process. About the British Embassy France Internships The British Embassy in Paris is part of the UK s global diplomatic network and represents British political, economic and consular interests overseas. Interns will work alongside experienced professionals and contribute to projects, events, policy work and international engagement involving the UK and France. The programme is designed for motivated students and graduates interested in areas such as: Diplomacy and international relations European and EU affairs Public policy Political and economic affairs Migration and borders National security Communications and public diplomacy International engagement Applicants from different academic and professional backgrounds are encouraged to apply, with emphasis placed on motivation, potential and skills. Available Internship Teams 1. Economics and Political Section (EPS) The Economics and Political Section works with French government institutions, academia, businesses and civil society organisations to strengthen cooperation between the UK and France. The section covers: Bilateral and Political Affairs Economic, Social and Sustainability Policy European Affairs Science and Technology The successful intern will work within the European Affairs team during a period in which the UK is seeking to strengthen its relations with France, the European Union and wider European partners. Responsibilities may include: Monitoring and analysing political, EU and economic developments Conducting research on priority policy issues Drafting briefings, reports and policy updates Supporting strategic engagement with French stakeholders Assisting with Embassy events, ministerial visits and diplomatic engagements Providing administrative and project support This placement is particularly suited to candidates interested in research, current affairs and the relationship between policy decisions and international relations. 2. National Security and Foreign Policy Section (NSFP) The National Security and Foreign Policy Section focuses on major international challenges and works closely with French institutions and international partners. Its areas of work include: Foreign and Development Policy Migration and Borders National Security Interns will support work that helps UK decision-makers understand French perspectives on foreign policy, migration and security matters. Possible responsibilities include: Researching and analysing French policy developments Preparing reports and briefings Supporting strategic stakeholder engagement Working with think tanks and policy experts Assisting with Embassy events and high-level meetings Working with colleagues across the FCDO, Ministry of Defence, Cabinet Office and wider UK Government network The placement is particularly relevant for candidates interested in international relations, global affairs, security and public policy. 3. Communications and Engagement Team The Communications and Engagement Team works across France to communicate UK priorities to different audiences and support public diplomacy. The team includes: Media and press relations Ministerial and VIP visits Public diplomacy Outreach programmes Cultural engagement Flagship events The successful intern will primarily support the Europe Regional Programme Fund , helping coordinate projects that advance UK priorities and strengthen UK-France relations. Responsibilities may include: Supporting programme and project management Monitoring project delivery, outcomes and financial compliance Maintaining programme records and documentation Supporting governance meetings Working with external partners, media organisations and stakeholders Assisting with public diplomacy events Supporting media monitoring and reporting Contributing to social media and communications activities Supporting high-level visits and diplomatic engagements Eligibility and Requirements Applicants should demonstrate the following: Excellent written and spoken French and English , with a minimum C1 CEFR level An internship agreement known as a “Convention de stage” Interest in Europe/EU affairs, migration, communications and/or UK-France relations Interest in politics and working in an international environment Ability to work effectively as part of a team Drive, enthusiasm and the ability to deliver Strong research and problem-solving skills Ability to work independently and find creative solutions Excellent communication skills Strong organisational and attention-to-detail skills Flexibility to support wider Embassy priorities Confidence using Microsoft Office Candidates must also currently hold an independent right to live and work in France and be able to maintain that right throughout the contract. Internship Details Organisation: British Embassy in France Location: Paris, France Position: Intern Number of vacancies: 3 Duration: 5 months Start date: 2 November 2026 Working arrangement: Full-time Working hours: 35 hours per week Salary: €1,000 gross per month Additional condition: Meal contribution Application deadline: 2 September 2026 The position also allows some flexible and remote working, although the jobholder is expected to work from the office at least 60% of the week and more frequently when required. Application Requirements Applications must be submitted in English and must clearly indicate all nationalities held by the applicant. Successful candidates will undergo professional background checks and security clearance. Applicants should also note that the position requires the successful candidate to provide documentation for security and background checks, including identification, recent criminal-record documentation for relevant countries of residence, proofs of address and references. The British Embassy states that the internship is locally recruited and governed by applicable French employment conditions. It is not an entry point into the UK s Diplomatic Service . Important Application Information The application deadline is 2 September 2026 at 23:55 , using the time zone of the country where the vacancy has arisen. Applicants are advised to allow sufficient time to complete and submit their applications before the deadline. Applicants should also ensure that their application authentically reflects their own experiences. The Embassy states that AI tools may only be used for limited tasks such as formatting consistency and keyword relevance, while personal narratives and responses must genuinely reflect the applicant s own professional journey and achievements. Applications for Country Based Staff positions with the British Government must be submitted through the official tal.net recruitment platform . The Embassy warns that applications submitted through other websites will not be received. Conclusion The British Embassy France Internships 2026 provide three internship opportunities for candidates seeking practical exposure to diplomacy, European affairs, foreign policy, national security, communications and public diplomacy. With placements across three specialised teams, the programme offers interns the opportunity to contribute to the work of the British Embassy while developing experience in an international government environment. Interested candidates should carefully review the requirements, confirm their right to live and work independently in France, and submit their application before the 2 September 2026 deadline. title: NASA Spring 2027 Internship in USA | Graduate Internship at Langley Research Center
summary: NASA is offering a Spring 2027 internship for graduate students interested in government relations, public policy, stakeholder engagement, strategic communications, partnerships, and aerospace innovation. The internship will support NASA’s regional partnerships and stakeholder engagement activities at NASA’s Langley Research Center (LaRC) in Hampton, Virginia. Interns will gain hands-on experience researching and coordinating with government, academic, industry, and advocacy partners while contributing to initiatives that support NASA’s mission. The internship is an in-person opportunity for U.S. citizens at the graduate master’s level, with registration open until September 14, 2026. About the NASA Spring 2027 Internship NASA internships provide educational, hands-on opportunities that allow undergraduate and graduate students aged 16 and above to gain research and operational experience related to NASA. This particular Spring 2027 internship focuses on regional partnerships and stakeholder engagement. The selected intern will work at the intersection of government relations, public-sector collaboration, and aerospace innovation . The intern will support research, coordination and strategic communications involving NASA’s state, local, academic and industry partners. Through the experience, the intern will contribute directly to ongoing partnership initiatives designed to advance NASA’s mission. Project Objectives The internship is designed to help strengthen NASA’s regional engagement efforts. The intern will contribute to the following objectives: * Map and analyse key external stakeholders across government, academia, industry and advocacy organisations. * Support partnership development activities and track engagement efforts. * Assist with preparations for meetings, events and external briefings. * Organise information that can support leadership decision-making and outreach strategies. Key Responsibilities The selected intern will be expected to undertake a range of research, coordination and communications responsibilities. These include: Conducting Background Research The intern will research regional partners, consortia and initiatives that align with NASA priorities. This will involve gathering and analysing information that can help NASA better understand regional aerospace, research and innovation ecosystems. Developing Stakeholder Tracking Tools The intern will develop and maintain stakeholder tracking tools, contact lists and engagement summaries. These resources will help organise information about external partners and support ongoing engagement activities. Preparing Briefing Materials The intern will draft briefing materials, talking points and concise summaries for internal use. This work will require the ability to synthesise information and communicate key findings clearly. Supporting Meetings and Events The intern will assist with meeting preparation, including developing agendas, recording notes and preparing follow-up documentation. The intern may also support planning and coordination for regional meetings, conferences and other partner engagements. Analysing Regional Trends The intern will analyse trends across regional aerospace, research and innovation ecosystems and summarise the findings for relevant stakeholders. Internship Deliverables By the end of the internship, the selected intern is expected to produce several deliverables based on their work. These include: * A stakeholder landscape overview covering a defined region or topic area. * A concise engagement tracker or reference tool for partnership activities. * Written briefing materials or summaries used to support leadership or external engagement. * A short final report or presentation outlining key insights, outcomes and recommendations. Learning Outcomes The NASA internship will provide the selected student with practical exposure to NASA’s partnership and external engagement processes. The intern will gain: * Exposure to NASA’s partnership strategy and external engagement processes. * Experience working in a federal government environment. * Skills in stakeholder analysis. * Professional writing and strategic coordination skills. * Insight into how public-sector partnerships contribute to science, technology and innovation. Preferred Skills and Interests Applicants should have interests or abilities relevant to the focus of the internship. Preferred skills and interests include: * Strong written and verbal communication skills. * Interest in government relations, public policy, partnerships or STEM-related fields. * Ability to synthesise information and present it clearly. * Strong organisational skills and attention to detail. * Ability to work independently and collaboratively. Eligibility Requirements The opportunity is listed for students at the Graduate Master s academic level . Preferred Majors The internship lists the following preferred academic areas: Business, Management, Marketing and Related Fields * Business, Management, Marketing and Related Support Services, Other * Business/Commerce, General * Business/Managerial Economics * Marketing, Other Communications and Public Relations * Public Relations, Advertising and Applied Communication, Other Public Administration and Public Policy * Public Administration * Public Administration and Social Service Professions, Other * Public Policy Analysis, General Applicants whose academic backgrounds align with these areas may find the internship particularly relevant. How to Apply for the NASA Spring 2027 Internship Interested applicants should visit NASA’s official internship platform to explore available opportunities and begin the application process. Step 1 : Visit the NASA Internship Website Go to the official NASA internship website: Step 2 : Review the Opportunity Search for the Spring 2027 internship focused on regional partnerships and stakeholder engagement at Langley Research Center. Review the eligibility requirements, preferred academic areas and project information carefully. Step 3 : Prepare Your Application Ensure that your application materials accurately demonstrate your relevant academic background, communication abilities, research experience, organisational skills and interest in government relations, public policy, partnerships or STEM-related fields. Step 4 : Submit Before the Deadline Complete and submit the application by September 14, 2026 . Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications in case additional information or documents are required. Location The internship will be based at NASA’s Langley Research Center (LaRC) in Hampton, Virginia . The activity format is listed as in-person , meaning the selected intern will participate from the designated NASA location. Why Apply? This internship provides an opportunity for a graduate student to gain practical experience within a federal government environment while working on issues involving regional partnerships, stakeholder engagement, public-sector collaboration and aerospace innovation. The intern will also have the opportunity to develop professional skills in stakeholder analysis, research, writing, strategic coordination and information synthesis while contributing to work connected to NASA’s mission. Conclusion The NASA Spring 2027 Regional Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement Internship is an in-person graduate internship at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia. The opportunity is particularly suited to students interested in government relations, public policy, public administration, communications, partnerships, business, marketing and STEM-related fields. The selected intern will support stakeholder research, partnership activities, briefing preparation, meeting coordination and analysis of regional aerospace and innovation ecosystems. Eligible applicants should review the official opportunity carefully and submit their applications before the September 14, 2026 deadline. Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage . title: Heilbronn AI Fellowship in Germany | €2,800 Monthly Fellowship for International Researchers
summary: Applications are now open for the Heilbronn AI Fellowship , a new research fellowship programme launched by the DAAD German Academic Exchange Service and the Dieter Schwarz Foundation . The fellowship offers outstanding international PhD candidates and postdoctoral researchers the opportunity to undertake an Artificial Intelligence research project at an eligible institution on Bildungscampus Heilbronn in Germany. Fellows will join Heilbronn s growing AI ecosystem, which brings together academic research, industry collaboration, digital infrastructure, technology transfer, and entrepreneurship. The fellowship provides €2,800 per month , together with support for health, accident and personal liability insurance and a lump sum towards international travel costs. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis , meaning there is no fixed application deadline . About the Heilbronn AI Fellowship The Heilbronn AI Fellowship is designed to attract outstanding international researchers working in Artificial Intelligence and related fields to Heilbronn, Germany. The programme supports research stays at eligible universities and research institutions located on Bildungscampus Heilbronn . In addition to conducting research, fellows will become part of an ecosystem connecting academic institutions with industry and innovation partners. The programme encourages technology transfer, practical applications of AI research, and engagement with entrepreneurial and startup ecosystems. The fellowship aims to connect international research talent with Heilbronn s growing network of research, industry, and innovation partners. Who Can Apply? The fellowship is open to international PhD candidates and postdoctoral researchers who meet the programme requirements. Eligible applicants include: International PhD candidates in the final year before their dissertation defense. International postdoctoral researchers who obtained their doctorate no more than five years ago. Researchers with a strong academic background in Artificial Intelligence or a related field. Applicants affiliated with a university or non-university research institution. Applicants planning to undertake a research project at an eligible host institution on Bildungscampus Heilbronn. The fellowship is particularly suited to researchers whose work aligns with Artificial Intelligence and related areas. What Can Be Funded? The fellowship provides funding for a research stay in Artificial Intelligence or a related field at an eligible host institution in Heilbronn. During the research stay, fellows will have the opportunity to work within an environment combining: Academic research Industry collaboration Advanced digital infrastructure Technology transfer Innovation Entrepreneurship AI applications The programme is intended to support research that contributes to scientific knowledge while encouraging connections between research and real-world applications. Eligible Host Institutions Research stays can be undertaken at eligible universities and research institutions located on Bildungscampus Heilbronn . These include: DHBW Center for Advanced Studies The DHBW Center for Advanced Studies offers postgraduate study and research opportunities within the Baden-Württemberg Cooperative State University network. DHBW Heilbronn DHBW Heilbronn is part of the Baden-Württemberg Cooperative State University and is one of the institutions participating in the Heilbronn research ecosystem. Ferdinand-Steinbeis-Institute The Ferdinand-Steinbeis-Institute is an interdisciplinary research institution involved in applied research and innovation. Fraunhofer HNFIZ Fraunhofer HNFIZ is among the research institutions eligible to host research projects under the fellowship. Heilbronn University of Applied Sciences Heilbronn University of Applied Sciences is another eligible institution located on Bildungscampus Heilbronn. TUM Campus Heilbronn The Technical University of Munich (TUM) Campus Heilbronn is also an eligible host institution for fellowship research projects. Applicants should establish contact with an eligible host institution and develop their research project in cooperation with the proposed host. Duration of the Fellowship Funding is available for research stays lasting between 1 and 12 months . The fellowship cannot normally be extended. Special circumstances may be considered individually. The funding is available during the programme s funding period. Fellowship Benefits The Heilbronn AI Fellowship provides financial support to successful fellows. The main benefits include: €2,800 monthly fellowship instalment Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance A lump sum towards international travel costs Additional support may also be available in certain circumstances. These may include: Support for additional costs arising from a disability or chronic illness, subject to individual assessment. Family benefits for fellows whose funding period exceeds six months, subject to eligibility. Other support related to special circumstances, assessed on a case-by-case basis. Selection Process Selection is conducted through a single-stage evaluation based on the submitted application documents. Applications are jointly prepared by the applicant and the proposed host institution and are evaluated by independent experts in the relevant research fields. Experts are appointed by the DAAD, while partner institutions may propose candidates. Individuals with conflicts of interest or a supervisory relationship with an applicant are excluded from the evaluation process. Funding is awarded only after a positive evaluation by the appointed experts. Selection Criteria Applications are assessed according to several key criteria. Academic Qualification The selection process considers: Academic performance General grade point average Development of academic performance Dissertation grade Course of study and doctorate Academic achievements after graduation Publications Lectures and conference papers Quality of the Research Project The proposed research project is assessed based on: Originality of the research proposal Topicality and relevance of the project Quality of preparation Suitability of the selected host institution Initial contact with the host institution Relevance for application and technology transfer Feasibility of the research plan Consistency of the proposed schedule Suitability of the applicant s profile for the project Potential for personal and professional development Potential for longer-term research cooperation The selection process also considers equal-opportunity aspects that applicants can provide information about in the application form. Application Process Applications for the Heilbronn AI Fellowship are submitted online through the DAAD portal . Applicants should work with their proposed host institution when preparing the application and research project. Step 1: Identify an Eligible Host Institution Applicants should identify an eligible institution on Bildungscampus Heilbronn that is suitable for their proposed AI research project. Step 2: Develop Your Research Project Prepare a strong research proposal that clearly explains the project s objectives, relevance, methodology, feasibility, and potential contribution. Step 3: Prepare the Required Documents Applicants should ensure that all required application documents are prepared according to the DAAD requirements. Step 4: Submit the Application Online Applications must be submitted through the DAAD online application portal . An application is considered valid only when the required documents have been submitted through the portal by the relevant application time. If a required document is unavailable at the time of submission, applicants should explain the reason and indicate when the document will be provided. Application Deadline The Heilbronn AI Fellowship operates on a rolling application basis . There is no fixed application deadline. Applicants should therefore review the official fellowship information and application requirements and submit their applications according to the applicable programme and funding conditions. Important Application Information Only one application per applicant can be considered at any given time. Simultaneous applications cannot be processed. Applicants should carefully review all requirements before submitting their application and ensure that the research project is appropriately connected to an eligible host institution. Why Apply for the Heilbronn AI Fellowship? The fellowship offers international AI researchers an opportunity to undertake research in one of Germany s growing AI and innovation ecosystems. By connecting researchers with universities, research institutions, industry partners, and innovation networks, the programme provides a setting for academic research as well as collaboration and technology transfer. Researchers can use the fellowship period to advance their projects while developing connections that may contribute to longer-term research and professional opportunities. Conclusion The Heilbronn AI Fellowship offers outstanding international PhD candidates and postdoctoral researchers the opportunity to conduct AI research in Heilbronn, Germany , while becoming part of a growing ecosystem of academic, industry, and innovation partners. Successful fellows can receive €2,800 per month , insurance-related support, and a travel allowance for research stays lasting 1 to 12 months . The fellowship is open to international PhD candidates in the final year before their dissertation defense and postdoctoral researchers who obtained their doctorate no more than five years ago. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis , with no fixed deadline. Interested researchers should review the official DAAD requirements, identify an eligible host institution, develop their research proposal, and submit their application through the DAAD portal. Monthly for AI research. Rolling applications. Discover more on the OFY Webpage . title: Next Gen Initiative 2026: Fellowship for Young African Women – Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Center
summary: Are you a young African woman passionate about public leadership, governance, development, gender, health, law, or public policy ? The Next Gen Initiative 2026 is an opportunity for emerging women leaders from selected African countries to strengthen their leadership skills, gain practical public leadership experience, and build networks for lasting impact. The Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Presidential Center for Women and Development (EJS Center) is launching the Next Gen Initiative, its flagship leadership program for emerging African women leaders. The 12-month fellowship is designed to prepare promising young women for future leadership roles through leadership development, mentorship, immersive learning, and hands-on public leadership placements alongside Amujae Leaders . Next Gen Initiative 2026 Fellowship The program aims to cultivate Africa s next generation of women public leaders by providing fellows with the exposure, experience, mentorship, and support needed to advance their leadership journeys. Throughout the 12-month fellowship, participants will have opportunities to: Develop leadership and professional skills Receive mentorship from experienced women leaders Gain practical exposure to public leadership Participate in immersive learning experiences Build professional networks across Africa Work alongside Amujae Leaders Strengthen their capacity to drive social and public impact Develop perspectives and skills to contribute to positive change in their communities and countries Who Can Apply? The Next Gen Initiative is seeking purpose-driven young African women who demonstrate leadership potential and a strong commitment to public service. Applicants should demonstrate: Integrity and strong ethical values Leadership potential Curiosity and willingness to learn Resilience and determination A strong commitment to public service A clear interest in advancing positive change in their communities and countries A commitment to developing their long-term leadership trajectory Eligibility Criteria To be eligible for the Next Gen Initiative 2026 , applicants must: Be 25–35 years old as of October 1, 2026 . Hold an undergraduate degree . Have at least three years of relevant and consistent professional experience . Have professional experience in public policy, law, development, gender, health, governance, or a related field . Demonstrate strong leadership potential, integrity, and commitment to public service. Show a clear interest in developing their leadership trajectory and contributing to positive change in their country and across Africa. Eligible Countries The inaugural Next Gen Initiative cohort is open only to citizens of the following countries : 🇰🇪 Kenya 🇱🇸 Lesotho 🇱🇷 Liberia 🇳🇬 Nigeria 🇸🇱 Sierra Leone Applicants from countries outside this list are not eligible for the inaugural cohort. Fellowship Duration The Next Gen Initiative is a 12-month fellowship program combining leadership development, mentorship, learning opportunities, and practical public leadership experience. Fellowship Stipend and Support Selected fellows will receive a monthly stipend for the duration of the 12-month fellowship to support their participation in the program. The fellowship therefore provides both professional development and financial support to help selected participants fully engage in the program. Why Apply for the Next Gen Initiative? The Next Gen Initiative offers emerging African women leaders an opportunity to gain practical leadership experience, mentorship, professional networks, and exposure to public leadership . For women seeking careers in government, public policy, development, governance, gender equality, health, law, or other public service fields , the fellowship can provide valuable experience and connections to support their leadership journey. APPLY NOW: Next Gen Initiative Application Form How to Apply for the Next Gen Initiative 2026 Eligible candidates are encouraged to complete the Next Gen Initiative Application Form and provide the required information demonstrating their leadership experience, professional background, commitment to public service, and aspirations for positive change. title: COY21 2026: Global Youth Climate Conference in Türkiye – Delegate Applications Now Open
summary: Are you a young climate leader looking to participate in global climate discussions and contribute to the youth agenda ahead of COP31 ? Applications are now open for the 21st Conference of Children and Youth on Climate Change (COY21) , taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 5–7 November 2026 . Organized by YOUNGO , the official Children and Youth Constituency of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) , COY21 will bring together young people from around the world to build capacity, strengthen climate advocacy, develop practical skills, and contribute to the global youth climate agenda ahead of COP31. What Is COY21? The Conference of Youth (COY) is the world s largest and most significant gathering of children and young people focused on climate change. COY serves as an important preparatory space for young people before the annual UN Climate Change Conference. Through workshops, training, discussions and advocacy activities, participants develop the knowledge and skills needed to engage meaningfully in international climate policy processes. COY21 2026 will provide young people with opportunities to: Build knowledge and leadership skills on climate change. Participate in climate advocacy and youth diplomacy. Engage in negotiation-aligned sessions ahead of COP31. Share local and regional perspectives on climate challenges. Contribute to the global youth climate agenda. Connect with young climate leaders from around the world. Prepare collectively for participation in the COP31 process. COY21 Delegate Opportunity 2026 Applications are now being invited from motivated young leaders interested in joining the COY21 Delegation . Selected delegates will represent their communities, countries or regions, participate in international youth climate diplomacy, and contribute to shaping global youth priorities ahead of COP31 . Who Can Apply? To be eligible for the COY21 Delegate opportunity , applicants must: Be under 35 years old at the time of COY21. Demonstrate an interest in or engagement with climate action, youth leadership or policy advocacy at local, regional or international level. Commit to participating actively in pre- and post-COY21 delegation preparations, meetings and follow-up activities . Be able to self-fund travel to Antalya, Türkiye . CLICK HERE TO APPLY What Are COY21 Delegates Expected to Contribute? COY21 is seeking diverse, passionate and engaged young people who can: Represent their community, country or region internationally. Bring strong local perspectives to COY21 discussions and outcomes. Contribute to climate justice, climate policy and grassroots climate action . Share experiences and perspectives from their communities. Take knowledge, connections and commitments from COY21 back home to strengthen climate action. Diversity and Representation The final selection process will seek to ensure balanced representation across gender, geographic regions and thematic expertise . This means young people from diverse backgrounds and with different experiences in climate action, policy, advocacy and grassroots work are encouraged to apply. Important Application Requirement The use of AI to complete the application form is prohibited. Applications may be disqualified if it is determined that AI was used to complete the form. Applicants should therefore ensure that their responses accurately reflect their own experiences, perspectives and ideas. COY21 2026 Key Details Opportunity COY21 Delegate Event 21st Conference of Children and Youth on Climate Change Location Antalya, Türkiye Dates 5–7 November 2026 Age limit Under 35 Focus Climate action, youth leadership, advocacy and policy Travel Self-funded Deadline 5 September 2026 How to Apply for COY21 2026 Young climate leaders interested in joining the COY21 delegation should submit their Expression of Interes t before the deadline. Application deadline: 5 September 2026 For questions about the application or delegation, contact: liaisons@climatecoy.com admin@climatecoy.com Frequently Asked Questions What is COY21? COY21 is the 21st Conference of Children and Youth on Climate Change, bringing young people together ahead of COP31 to build capacity, advocate for climate action and contribute to the global youth climate agenda. Where will COY21 2026 take place? COY21 will take place in Antalya, Türkiye , from 5–7 November 2026 . Who can apply for the COY21 delegation? Young people under 35 years old who demonstrate engagement or interest in climate action, youth leadership or policy advocacy can apply. Is COY21 fully funded? title: Nonprofit Open Source Partnership 2026: Free Technical Support, 800 Hours of Development and Open Source Transformation for Nonprofits
summary: The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is offering a valuable opportunity for selected nonprofit organizations to transform their existing software and technology projects into publicly accessible, licensed and well-documented open source tools — at no cost to participating organizations. The partnership brings together Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward to support a small group of technology-focused nonprofits with the technical expertise, student developer capacity and industry mentorship needed to prepare software for open source use or strengthen projects that are already part of the open source ecosystem. As part of the program, each selected nonprofit will receive a dedicated team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers who will work on the organization s project for 16 weeks . The program represents approximately 800 hours of technical work per team , supported by weekly check-ins, technical guidance, project management assistance and team coaching. The program is particularly relevant for nonprofits that have developed useful technology but lack the time, staff capacity or specialised expertise required to properly license, document, package and maintain that technology as an open source resource. Applications for the program close on September 9, 2026 . Nonprofit Open Source Partnership 2026 at a Glance Program: Nonprofit Open Source Partnership Organizing partners: Bloomberg, Develop for Good, CodeDay and Fast Forward Target applicants: Selected technology-focused nonprofit organizations Project focus: Open sourcing an existing nonprofit software tool or contributing to an existing open source project Technical support: Eight college student volunteer developers per nonprofit Program duration: 16 weeks Technical contribution: Approximately 800 hours per team Industry mentorship: Bloomberg employee volunteers Open source guidance: CodeDay Program support: Develop for Good Cost: No cost to participating nonprofits Nonprofit application deadline: September 9, 2026 Selection notification: October 2, 2026 Program kickoff: October 25, 2026 Final delivery: February 20, 2027 What Is the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership? Many nonprofit organizations build or use technology to deliver their missions, but creating software and preparing it for open source distribution are two different challenges. A nonprofit may have an existing application, platform, internal tool or other technology that could potentially benefit other organizations. However, making that technology genuinely open source involves much more than publishing code online. The organization may need to address: Software licensing Technical documentation Code organization Developer onboarding Project contribution processes Technical maintenance User documentation Open source best practices Project management Quality assurance Collaboration with external developers These tasks require time and specialised technical knowledge that many nonprofits may not have available internally. The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is designed to help close this gap. Through the partnership, participating organizations receive a dedicated team of student developers and support from experienced professionals who can help turn an existing technology project into a more accessible and reusable open source resource. Who Is Behind the Program? The initiative is a collaboration between four organizations: Bloomberg Bloomberg is participating in the partnership through employee volunteers who will provide guidance and mentorship to participating nonprofit projects. Develop for Good Develop for Good provides the student development teams and program support. The organization will run weekly check-ins with participating students and provide structured support covering technical work, project management and team coaching. CodeDay CodeDay will provide guidance on open source best practices , helping participating nonprofits understand how to prepare their projects for open source use. Fast Forward Fast Forward is also part of the partnership, contributing to an initiative designed to strengthen technology capacity within the nonprofit sector. Together, these organizations provide a combination of student technical talent, professional mentorship, open source expertise and program management support. What Will Selected Nonprofits Receive? Selected organizations will receive several forms of support throughout the 16-week program. 1. A Dedicated Team of Eight Student Developers Each participating nonprofit will receive a team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers . The students will dedicate their time to the nonprofit s selected project throughout the 16-week program. This gives nonprofits access to a substantial pool of technical capacity without the financial cost associated with hiring a conventional software development team. 2. Approximately 800 Hours of Technical Work The program estimates that each team will contribute approximately 800 hours of technical work . This can provide significant development capacity for a nonprofit that may otherwise struggle to dedicate internal resources to an open source initiative. The exact nature of the work will depend on the organization s project and the objectives established for the program. Potential work could involve preparing an existing tool for open source publication, improving documentation or contributing to an existing open source project. 3. Weekly Program Check-Ins Develop for Good will conduct weekly check-ins with students throughout the program. These check-ins are designed to help teams remain focused, address challenges and maintain progress toward the project s objectives. 4. Technical Support Participating teams will receive structured technical support to help them move their projects forward. This can be especially valuable for organizations that have a strong mission and a useful technology product but do not have extensive internal software engineering capacity. 5. Project Management Support The partnership also includes project management assistance. This helps keep the work organized and ensures that the student development team and nonprofit point-of-contact remain aligned on priorities, deliverables and timelines. 6. Team Coaching Teams will receive coaching designed to support effective collaboration and project execution. Because the program involves nonprofit staff, student developers and industry mentors, structured coaching can help ensure that different participants remain coordinated throughout the 16-week engagement. 7. Open Source Best-Practices Guidance CodeDay will provide guidance on open source best practices. This is particularly important for nonprofits that are making the transition from an internally developed or privately maintained tool to a publicly accessible project. 8. Bloomberg Employee Mentorship Participating nonprofits will receive weekly guidance from experienced Bloomberg employee volunteers. These mentors are described as being invested in the success of the projects and can provide an additional professional perspective throughout the program. 9. A Publicly Accessible and Documented Final Product One of the most important outcomes is a finished project that is intended to be: Publicly accessible Properly licensed Documented Ready for the nonprofit to use Potentially useful to other organizations This can extend the impact of a nonprofit s technology beyond its immediate internal use. What Does Open Source Mean for Participating Nonprofits? Open source software is software whose source code is made available under a license that allows others to access, use and, depending on the license, modify and redistribute it under defined conditions. For a nonprofit, making a tool open source can create opportunities for other organizations, developers and communities to benefit from technology that might otherwise remain limited to the organization that originally developed it. However, simply uploading software to a public repository does not necessarily mean that a project is ready for meaningful open source collaboration. A well-prepared open source project generally needs appropriate licensing, clear documentation and enough structure for other users or developers to understand how the project works and how they can engage with it. That is the gap this partnership is intended to address. Learn more HERE What Types of Projects Can Participate? The program is designed for nonprofits with an existing technology project that is ready to be open sourced or that needs support to contribute to an existing open source project. A nonprofit may therefore consider applying if it has: An existing software tool it wants to make open source A technology project that needs improved documentation A software project that needs preparation for public release An existing open source project that requires development support A technical project that could benefit from a dedicated student development team The organization should have a sufficiently defined project for the student developers and mentors to work on during the 16-week program. Apply HERE What Does the Nonprofit Need to Contribute? Although the program is offered at no cost to participating organizations, selected nonprofits are expected to commit time and resources in the form of staff participation. Each participating nonprofit should plan for approximately: 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks from a designated point-of-contact. The nonprofit point-of-contact will participate in activities such as: Regular check-ins Providing feedback Collaborating with student developers Working with industry mentors Answering project-related questions Helping clarify priorities Reviewing project progress Supporting decision-making when necessary This commitment is important because the student developers and mentors need a knowledgeable representative from the nonprofit to provide context and feedback. How Much Time Should a Nonprofit Expect to Commit? The stated commitment is approximately 2–3 hours per week for 16 weeks . Over the entire program period, this represents approximately 32–48 hours of point-of-contact involvement. Organizations should therefore select someone who can consistently participate throughout the program. A nonprofit that cannot provide a reliable point-of-contact may struggle to take full advantage of the technical resources being provided. What Does the Program Cost? The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership is offered at no cost to participating organizations . This is one of the program s major advantages because nonprofits can receive substantial technical support without having to pay for a professional software development team. The program combines volunteer student developers with industry mentors and structured organizational support to provide the technical capacity needed to advance participating projects. Why Open Source Can Matter for Nonprofits Transforming nonprofit software into open source can have benefits beyond the immediate project. A well-documented and publicly accessible tool can potentially: Allow other nonprofits to use the technology. Encourage collaboration among developers. Reduce duplication of technology development. Create opportunities for external contributions. Increase the visibility of the organization s technical work. Make the software easier for other organizations to evaluate and adopt. Build a community around a useful technology project. Extend the impact of technology developed for a specific nonprofit mission. The potential impact depends on the quality of the project, the needs of the wider community and the nonprofit s ability to maintain and support the software after the program concludes. Program Timeline The Nonprofit Open Source Partnership has a defined timeline from application through final delivery. September 9, 2026 — Applications Close This is the deadline for nonprofit organizations to submit their applications. Organizations interested in participating should complete their application before this date. October 2, 2026 — Selected Nonprofits Notified Organizations selected to participate will be notified on this date. October 25, 2026 — Program Kickoff The program officially begins with the kickoff on October 25, 2026. This marks the beginning of the 16-week collaboration involving the nonprofit, student developers and mentors. February 20, 2027 — Final Delivery The program is scheduled to conclude with final delivery on February 20, 2027. By this stage, participating teams will have worked toward completing the agreed project objectives. How to Apply for the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership Nonprofit organizations interested in participating should submit an application through the program s online application form. Application deadline: September 9, 2026. Apply for the Nonprofit Open Source Partnership Before applying, organizations should make sure they understand the program requirements and can commit the necessary staff time for the entire 16-week period. How Nonprofits Can Prepare a Strong Application Although the provided information does not specify a detailed scoring rubric, organizations can prepare by clearly defining the project they want the program to support. 1. Identify the technology project Determine which existing tool or project you want the student development team to work on. The project should be sufficiently defined to explain what the team will be expected to accomplish. 2. Explain why the project should become open source Organizations should be prepared to explain the value of making their technology publicly accessible. Consider: Who could benefit from the software? The opportunity is especially relevant to nonprofit organizations that have an existing technology or software project and want technical assistance to make it open source or contribute to an existing open source project. How many student developers does each nonprofit receive? Each participating nonprofit receives a team of eight vetted and trained college student volunteer developers .
